data.narrative:
Lumaril is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield. The company has raised $12M to date. The comparable universe in Robotics & Manufacturing includes 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers, among them Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

The stage-progression method is applicable and forms the sole reliable triangulation point. Using total capital raised ($12M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of progression from Seed to the next stage yields $30M. The peer-median approach is not applicable; while 11 same-sector robotics companies exist in the dataset, the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) did not yield the minimum three comparable datapoints required for statistical confidence. A broad-sector median would introduce unacceptable selection bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered at $30M. This range reflects the standard deviation implicit in single-method triangulation and the variance typical of step-up multiples at the Seed-to-Series A transition. Key uncertainties include the limited peer set available for cross-validation and Lumaril's specific competitive positioning within the robotics sector relative to the identified comparables. Validation of this range would benefit from either additional Seed-stage comps or product-stage metrics once available.
